# Supplementary Table S26. Separation between adjacent indicator standards

Local separation varies across the tested standards, with reversed ordering in some conditions. Each interval reports its response change, slope per reference unit and response change divided by local measurement noise.

**Figure panels** 1b–d, 1f, 4a–c · [All Supplementary tables](README.md)

**Column definitions**

- `family` — Identifies initial indicator calibration in chemical standards or indicator validation in growth media.
- `cohort` — Calibration condition (sulfuric acid or thymol blue concentration) or growth medium used for this interval.
- `readout` — Indicator response used for the two standards. R and R&#42; are the measured and scatter-corrected pH ratios, and A380 and A&#42;380 are the measured and scatter-corrected 380 nm absorbances.
- `assay` — Identifies whether pH or iron concentration defines the standards.
- `reference_unit` — Unit of the reference values and the denominator of the secant slope. The scale is pH for pH standards, measured total Fe (mM) for initial iron calibration, or added Fe (mM) for iron in growth media.
- `interval_rank` — Position of the adjacent pair in increasing reference order within a plate, starting at 0 for the first pair.
- `scheduled_plate_n` — Number of physical microplates scheduled for this adjacent reference interval, including plates with an unavailable response.
- `reference_low` — Mean lower endpoint of the reference interval across the scheduled plates, in the stated reference unit.
- `reference_high` — Mean upper endpoint of the reference interval across the scheduled plates, in the stated reference unit.
- `response_change_n` — Number of physical plates with a finite response change for this interval.
- `response_change` — Mean across plates of the higher-reference standard’s mean response minus the lower-reference standard’s mean response, in ratio units for pH or AU for iron.
- `response_change_ci_low` — Lower limit of the pointwise 95% Student’s t confidence interval across plates for the mean signed response change.
- `response_change_ci_high` — Upper limit of the pointwise 95% Student’s t confidence interval across plates for the mean signed response change.
- `secant_sensitivity_n` — Number of physical plates with a finite slope between these adjacent reference levels.
- `secant_sensitivity` — Mean across plates of the signed response change divided by the reference interval width on that plate, in response units per reference unit.
- `secant_sensitivity_ci_low` — Lower limit of the pointwise 95% Student’s t confidence interval across plates for the mean slope between adjacent standards.
- `secant_sensitivity_ci_high` — Upper limit of the pointwise 95% Student’s t confidence interval across plates for the mean slope between adjacent standards.
- `change_over_noise_n` — Number of physical plates with a positive, finite ratio of absolute response change to combined technical-well SD.
- `change_over_noise` — Geometric mean across plates of the absolute response change divided by √(SD_low² + SD_high²), using the within-standard well SD at each endpoint. This ratio is dimensionless.
- `change_over_noise_ci_low` — Lower limit of the pointwise 95% confidence interval for the geometric mean change-to-noise ratio, calculated on the log scale with Student’s t and transformed back.
- `change_over_noise_ci_high` — Upper limit of the pointwise 95% confidence interval for the geometric mean change-to-noise ratio, calculated on the log scale with Student’s t and transformed back.
- `opposite_direction_plate_n` — Number of plates on which the pH-indicator response increased as pH increased or iron absorbance decreased as iron concentration increased.
- `interval_status` — Indicates whether the signed response change was estimated from at least two physical plates, observed on a single plate, or unavailable.

Blank numeric cells indicate quantities that were unavailable or inapplicable for that row.
